nodes.label: The Hair: Editor's Overview
nodes.summary: Editor's overview of Part 3.3 on hair. Notes that hair aesthetics are linked to viscoelastic properties of cuticle and cortex, that follicle biology (stem cells, hormones, graying) has advanced, and that hair care is moving to a holistic approach targeting live follicle cells with bioactives.

nodes.label: Hair
nodes.summary: Keratin fiber produced by the follicle; an optimized assembly of proteins, lipids and polysaccharides whose mature cells are dead but whose proteins retain biological activity.

nodes.label: Hair Cuticle
nodes.summary: Outer sheath of 5-11 stacked flat cuticle cells (~0.5 µm thick each) arranged like roof shingles that protects the cortex and controls lubricity, friction and optical properties.

nodes.label: Hair Cortex
nodes.summary: Bulk of the hair shaft made of cortical cells; provides strength, color and texture and is responsible for most mechanical properties.

nodes.label: Hair Follicle
nodes.summary: Small organ that produces and assembles hair cells into a fiber; one per hair, 80,000-150,000 on the scalp, regenerating cyclically.

nodes.label: Hair Growth Cycle
nodes.summary: Cyclic follicle activity of anagen (growth), catagen (regression) and telogen (rest), plus exogen and kenogen; disturbances underlie most hair growth disorders.

nodes.label: Hair Graying
nodes.summary: Loss of hair pigment with age (canities) due to decreased melanin production by follicle melanocytes; 74% of people aged 45-65 have gray hair.

nodes.label: Disulfide Bond
nodes.summary: Covalent cystine cross-link stabilizing the hair amorphous matrix and keratin structure; its scission underlies perms, relaxers and heat damage.

nodes.label: Eyelash
nodes.summary: Short (4-14 mm) curved hairs on the eyelids, 300-400 on the upper and 100-150 on the lower lid, with a short anagen phase.

nodes.label: Physical and Chemical Properties of Hair
nodes.summary: Reviews hair chemical composition, cortical, cuticle and medulla cells, viscoelasticity, shape memory, moisture sorption, optical properties and melanin, linking structure to hair function. Closes with follicle zones and the anagen-catagen-telogen life cycle, arguing hair proteins retain biological activity.

nodes.label: Keratin
nodes.summary: Helical structural protein providing mechanical strength; hair is rich in half-cystine, serine, glutamic acid and proline typical of keratin. Alpha (soft) keratins occur in hair, nails and skin; types I (acidic) and II (basic) are coiled in pairs.

nodes.label: Alpha Keratin
nodes.summary: Soft keratin with alpha-helical structure found in hair, nails, skin and wool; unfolds to beta configuration at 2-35% strain.

nodes.label: Beta Keratin
nodes.summary: Hard keratin typical of reptile claws and turtle shells; also the 'ladder or platelet' configuration hair keratin adopts when alpha helices unfold.

nodes.label: Cortical Cell
nodes.summary: Elongated spindle-shaped cells ~20 µm in diameter and ~100 µm long forming ~90% of hair; they synthesize keratin into intermediate filaments embedded in an amorphous matrix and determine mechanical properties.

nodes.label: Cuticle Cell
nodes.summary: Flat layered cells ~0.5 µm thick stacked 5-11 deep around the cortex; layers are F-layer (18-MEA), epicuticle, exocuticle, endocuticle and CMC; behavior is viscoelastic and moisture sensitive.

nodes.label: Hair Medulla
nodes.summary: Low-density porous central region of large cuboidal air-filled cells, discontinuous and present mostly in thicker hair; may aid thermal insulation and affects optical properties.

nodes.label: Intermediate Filament
nodes.summary: Crystalline keratin micro-fibrils (C phase) assembled in cortical cells and bound via disulfide bonds to the amorphous matrix to form macrofibrils; do not swell in water.

nodes.label: Amorphous Protein Matrix
nodes.summary: Disulfide cross-linked, non-crystalline protein phase (M phase) surrounding keratin microfibrils, with high- and low-sulfur regions and a water-plasticizable hydrophilic 'gel structure' plus a hydrophobic non-gel structure.

nodes.label: Gel Structure of the Amorphous Phase
nodes.summary: Hydrophilic, hydrogen-bonded part of the amorphous matrix (Feughelman's term) that absorbs water, is plasticized by moisture and stores temporary shapes such as water sets.

nodes.label: Cell Membrane Complex
nodes.summary: Extracellular 'cement' gluing cuticle and cortical cells, made of upper and lower beta (lipid) layers and a delta protein layer; the beta-delta junction is the weakest link and a diffusion path into the cortex.

nodes.label: 18-Methyl Eicosanoic Acid
nodes.summary: Branched fatty acid covalently attached to an ultra-high sulfur protein on the epicuticle forming the F layer; provides hair lubricity and hydrophobicity.

nodes.label: Epicuticle
nodes.summary: Cuticle layer ~120 nm thick beneath the 18-MEA monolayer; with the exocuticle it has the highest sulfur content in the fiber.

nodes.label: Exocuticle
nodes.summary: Highly cross-linked, sulfur-rich cuticle layer ~250 nm thick that makes the cuticle hard and abrasion resistant.

nodes.label: Endocuticle
nodes.summary: Non-cross-linked, negatively charged, water-swellable cuticle layer that is soft and acts as a viscoelastic cushion; site of cuticle failure when wet.

nodes.label: Hair Viscoelasticity
nodes.summary: Hair displays both elastic and viscous behavior: elastic under rapid deformation, viscous plus delayed recovery under prolonged deformation, owing to crystalline filaments in a plasticizable matrix.

nodes.label: Feughelman Two-Phase Model
nodes.summary: 1959 model by Max Feughelman treating keratin fibers as crystalline rods (C phase) in parallel with a water-sensitive amorphous matrix (M phase) to explain moisture-dependent viscoelasticity.

nodes.label: Hair Shape Memory
nodes.summary: Hair behaves as a thermoset, viscoelastic shape-memory biopolymer: it has a permanent shape that can be temporarily changed and later recovered.

nodes.label: Water Plasticization of Hair
nodes.summary: Water acts as the natural plasticizer of hair proteins, softening the gel structure of the amorphous phase so less force is needed to deform moist hair.

nodes.label: Alpha-to-Beta Keratin Transition
nodes.summary: Unfolding of alpha-helical keratin into the beta configuration at 2-35% strain (yield region); reversible when mechanical, usually irreversible when caused by heat or chemicals.

nodes.label: Hair Stress-Strain Curve
nodes.summary: Tensile curve of hair with Hookean region (0-2/5%), yield region (2-35%, keratin coil opening) and post-yield region (>35%, recrystallization) before break.

nodes.label: Glass Transition Temperature
nodes.summary: Temperature at which a hard amorphous polymer softens; hair Tg ~144°C relates to the amorphous matrix, and styling polymer Tg governs hold versus flaking.

nodes.label: Hair Melting Temperature
nodes.summary: Melting/denaturation temperature of hair's crystalline keratin phase, Tm ~156°C, detected as an endothermic DSC peak.

nodes.label: Hair Water Sorption Isotherm
nodes.summary: Sigmoidal water absorption isotherm of hair showing hysteresis; hair absorbs up to ~30% water at 100% RH, mostly in cortical cells.

nodes.label: Bound Water
nodes.summary: Water strongly bound to protein groups that stabilizes keratin secondary structure and remains even at zero RH; its loss with disulfide breakage causes denaturation.

nodes.label: Heat Buffering by Hair
nodes.summary: Moisture absorption and desorption by keratin releases and absorbs heat, letting hair and wool buffer scalp temperature; 1 kg of dry wool going 40-70% RH releases ~164 kJ.

nodes.label: Cuticle Cell Buckling
nodes.summary: Lifting and buckling of cuticle cells with breakage of CMC cement caused by elongation, blow-drying or hot irons; common at hair tips, partly viscoelastically reversible.

nodes.label: Light Interference Patterns
nodes.summary: Colorful microscopic thin-film interference patterns (LIPs) produced by lifted cuticle cells with air pockets; used as an optical microscopy technique to detect cuticle damage.

nodes.label: Hair Shine
nodes.summary: Specular reflection of light from smooth intact cuticle produces shine; lifted cuticles scatter light and make hair dull. Cuticle refractive index is ~1.53.

nodes.label: Melanin
nodes.summary: Polymeric pigment granules (~0.8 µm) built from DHI and DHICA that color hair and act as free radical scavengers, antioxidants and UV, heat and gamma-ray absorbers.

nodes.label: Eumelanin
nodes.summary: Brown to black melanin; brown eumelanin in low amounts gives blond hair, dark eumelanin gives dark hair; more photostable than pheomelanin.

nodes.label: Pheomelanin
nodes.summary: Yellow to red melanin found mainly in red hair; its synthesis also involves cysteine; less photostable than eumelanin.

nodes.label: Melanocyte
nodes.summary: Dendritic pigment cells in the follicle bulb that synthesize melanin and transfer it into cortical keratinocytes.

nodes.label: 5,6-Dihydroxyindole
nodes.summary: DHI; one of the chemical moieties (with DHICA) forming the melanin polymer.

nodes.label: Dermal Papilla
nodes.summary: Cluster of specialized fibroblast-derived cells at the follicle base; the follicle 'command center' that instructs proliferation, differentiation and hair size via growth factors.

nodes.label: Hair Follicle Stem Cell
nodes.summary: Epithelial stem cells residing in the bulge that regenerate the follicle each cycle and supply matrix keratinocytes.

nodes.label: Keratinization
nodes.summary: Hardening zone of the follicle where hair cells undergo apoptosis and their proteins are cross-linked by disulfide bonds, imprinting the permanent hair shape.

nodes.label: Anagen
nodes.summary: Growth phase of the follicle (2-6 years on scalp, 1-4 months for eyelashes) with intense matrix cell proliferation.

nodes.label: Catagen
nodes.summary: Regression phase lasting ~2-4 weeks in which follicle cells undergo apoptosis and a club fiber forms.

nodes.label: Telogen
nodes.summary: Resting phase of the follicle (~3 months on scalp, 4-8 months for eyelashes) after which the old hair is shed.

nodes.label: Apoptosis
nodes.summary: Programmed cell death; in hair, cells die in the follicle before beginning their functional life, and catagen is driven by apoptosis.

nodes.label: Ortho-Cortical Cell
nodes.summary: Cortical cell type absorbing less moisture than para cells; the higher the ortho content the curlier the hair.

nodes.label: Para-Cortical Cell
nodes.summary: Cortical cell type dominating straight hair; curly hair has para and ortho cells in separate cortex regions.

nodes.label: Hair Curl Shape
nodes.summary: Permanent straight, wavy or curly hair shape, associated with the ratio and arrangement of ortho- to para-cortical cells and imprinted in the follicle.

nodes.label: Sebaceous Gland
nodes.summary: Gland releasing sebum in concert with the follicle (pilosebaceous unit) to maintain the hair shaft; sebum output decreases with age.

nodes.label: Sebum
nodes.summary: Lipid secretion of sebaceous glands that hydrates the scalp and coats hair with a protective microfilm.

nodes.label: Androgenetic Alopecia
nodes.summary: Most common patterned hair loss: androgen-driven miniaturization of genetically predisposed follicles with shortened anagen and more telogen/kenogen.

nodes.label: Traction Alopecia
nodes.summary: Hair loss caused by external mechanical interference with follicle processes.

nodes.label: Trichorrhexis Nodosa
nodes.summary: Hair shaft defect listed among ailments caused by internal or external interference with hair growth and maintenance.

nodes.label: Pilosebaceous Unit
nodes.summary: Follicle plus sebaceous gland, targeted by major hormonal pathways and acting as a peripheral producer of steroid hormones, neuropeptides and neurotrophins.

nodes.label: Hair Damage
nodes.summary: Denaturation and bond breakage of hair proteins from heat, perms, bleaching, alkaline straightening, UV and mechanical fatigue, compromising moisture control and mechanical and optical properties.

nodes.label: Perceived Hair Dryness
nodes.summary: Subjective dryness linked more to cuticle surface roughness than to lack of cortical moisture; swatches at high RH scored higher dryness.

nodes.label: Wool
nodes.summary: Keratin fiber with cellular and protein architecture similar to hair; shares moisture and heat sorption behavior, so hair research draws on wool literature.

nodes.label: Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Polydimethylsiloxane silicone polymer; can fill cuticle air gaps or smooth the surface to enhance hair color and shine, and lowers inter-fiber friction.

nodes.label: UV Radiation
nodes.summary: Ultraviolet sunlight that oxidizes hair proteins, lipids and melanin, causing photo-aging, lightening, brittleness and follicle damage.

nodes.label: Oxidative Stress
nodes.summary: Imbalance of reactive oxygen species over antioxidant defenses; damages hair fibers and follicle melanocytes and is implicated in graying and hair aging.

nodes.label: Hair Follicle Anatomy and Biology
nodes.summary: Describes the anatomy of the anagen hair follicle (infundibulum, isthmus, bulge, bulb, dermal papilla, root sheaths) and the cycle of anagen, catagen, telogen, exogen and kenogen with its molecular regulators. Also covers follicle aging: graying via melanocyte loss and oxidative stress, and UV damage to follicles.

nodes.label: Lanugo Hair
nodes.summary: Very fine hair normally shed in utero or during the first weeks of life.

nodes.label: Vellus Hair
nodes.summary: Very short, nonpigmented, nonmedullated hairs covering the body; miniaturized follicles revert terminal to vellus hair.

nodes.label: Terminal Hair
nodes.summary: Large, usually pigmented and medullated hair, predominantly on the scalp, growing 0.3-0.4 mm per day.

nodes.label: Hair Follicle Bulge
nodes.summary: Region in the lower isthmus/ORS at the arrector pili insertion below the sebaceous gland harboring the follicle stem cell and melanocyte reservoir.

nodes.label: Hair Bulb
nodes.summary: Lowermost onion-shaped part of the anagen follicle, one of the most rapidly dividing tissues; the 'hair shaft factory' with matrix keratinocytes and melanocytes surrounding the dermal papilla.

nodes.label: Matrix Keratinocyte
nodes.summary: Proliferating keratinocytes of the bulb matrix that move upward and differentiate into the hair shaft and inner root sheath.

nodes.label: Inner Root Sheath
nodes.summary: Three-layer sheath (IRS cuticle, Huxley's and Henle's layers) whose keratins and trichohyalin support and mold the growing shaft and anchor it.

nodes.label: Outer Root Sheath
nodes.summary: Outermost follicle layer continuous with the epidermal basal layer, generated directly from the bulge; source of VEGF.

nodes.label: Trichohyalin
nodes.summary: Protein produced by IRS keratinocytes that acts as intracellular cement strengthening the inner root sheath.

nodes.label: Arrector Pili Muscle
nodes.summary: Adrenergically controlled muscle bundle that changes the follicle angle and makes hair stand up with cold or emotional stress; absent in eyelashes.

nodes.label: Trichocyte
nodes.summary: Terminally differentiated hair follicle keratinocytes making up the hair shaft.

nodes.label: Exogen
nodes.summary: Active, controlled shedding phase of the club fiber, typically near renewed anagen onset; 100-150 hairs shed per day is normal.

nodes.label: Kenogen
nodes.summary: Phase in which the follicle is empty after club fiber shedding and before new anagen; more frequent and longer in androgenetic alopecia.

nodes.label: Club Hair
nodes.summary: Fully keratinized dead hair with a club-shaped end formed during catagen and later shed in exogen.

nodes.label: Androgen
nodes.summary: Male hormones that convert vellus to terminal hair in beard/pubic regions but miniaturize frontal scalp follicles in predisposed individuals.

nodes.label: Dihydrotestosterone
nodes.summary: DHT, formed from testosterone by type II 5-alpha reductase; induces dermal papilla cells to secrete TGF-b1 and DKK-1 inhibiting keratinocyte growth; levels rise with age.

nodes.label: 5-Alpha Reductase
nodes.summary: Enzyme (type II) converting testosterone to DHT; elevated in dermal papilla cells of balding scalp.

nodes.label: Androgen Receptor
nodes.summary: Receptor found at higher levels in dermal papilla cells from balding scalp.

nodes.label: Transforming Growth Factor Beta 1
nodes.summary: TGF-b1 cytokine secreted by DHT-stimulated dermal papilla cells; promotes apoptosis and catagen, while TGF-b signals also activate stem cells at end of telogen.

nodes.label: DKK-1
nodes.summary: Dickkopf-1, secreted by DHT-induced dermal papilla cells; inhibits keratinocyte growth.

nodes.label: Insulin-Like Growth Factor 1
nodes.summary: IGF-1, anagen-maintaining growth factor produced by the dermal papilla with receptors in matrix cells; decreased expression precedes catagen.

nodes.label: Basic Fibroblast Growth Factor
nodes.summary: bFGF, anagen-maintaining factor produced by the dermal papilla; its decline is associated with catagen.

nodes.label: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor
nodes.summary: VEGF, potent angiogenic factor produced by ORS keratinocytes, upregulated with perifollicular vascularization during anagen.

nodes.label: Keratinocyte Growth Factor
nodes.summary: Growth factor supplied by the dermal papilla, critical for hair growth and melanogenesis (with BMP, HGF, IGF and SCF).

nodes.label: Stem Cell Factor
nodes.summary: Dermal papilla growth factor important for hair growth and melanogenesis; its decrease is one theory of graying.

nodes.label: Wnt Signaling
nodes.summary: Wnt signals from the dermal papilla activate quiescent follicle stem cells at the end of telogen to form a new follicle.

nodes.label: Interleukin-1 Alpha
nodes.summary: Apoptosis-promoting cytokine whose increased expression is associated with catagen.

nodes.label: Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha
nodes.summary: Apoptosis-promoting cytokine whose increased expression is associated with catagen.

nodes.label: Follicle Miniaturization
nodes.summary: Androgen-triggered conversion of terminal to vellus follicles in genetically predisposed frontal scalp, causing thinning and baldness.

nodes.label: Hair Loss
nodes.summary: Premature hair loss and excessive shedding from interruption of the hair cycle, leading to baldness; a multibillion-dollar market.

nodes.label: Melanogenesis
nodes.summary: Biochemical pathway in melanocytes producing melanin in melanosomes with tyrosinase as the rate-limiting enzyme; ceases during catagen.

nodes.label: Tyrosinase
nodes.summary: Rate-limiting enzyme of melanogenesis oxidizing tyrosine; H2O2-mediated oxidation of its methionine limits function and leads to graying.

nodes.label: Melanosome
nodes.summary: Cytoplasmic organelle where hair melanins form; transferred via dendrites to cortex and medulla keratinocytes.

nodes.label: Melanocyte Stem Cell
nodes.summary: Melanocyte reserve in the bulge region of the ORS that replenishes melanocytes each cycle; loss or failure to differentiate is a graying mechanism.

nodes.label: Reactive Oxygen Species
nodes.summary: ROS accumulate up to millimolar levels in gray/white scalp follicles and cause free radical damage to follicle melanocytes.

nodes.label: Catalase
nodes.summary: Antioxidant enzyme breaking down H2O2 to water and oxygen; expression is reduced in unpigmented and older follicles.

nodes.label: Hydrogen Peroxide
nodes.summary: H2O2; accumulates at millimolar levels in gray hair shafts causing oxidative stress; used at 3% to reoxidize disulfide bonds in perms and in permanent hair color.

nodes.label: Hair Follicle Aging
nodes.summary: Age-related loss of pigmentation, reduced follicle density, more telogen hairs, thinner shafts and slower growth.

nodes.label: Hair Fiber Diameter
nodes.summary: Shaft thickness, which decreases with follicle aging; peaks ~age 20 in men and mid-40s in women.

nodes.label: Circadian Clock
nodes.summary: Molecular oscillatory system proposed as a candidate for the clock controlling anagen duration.

nodes.label: Hair Aging: Protection and Repair
nodes.summary: Explains intrinsic and extrinsic hair aging and its signs: thinning, graying, dryness, loss of shine and manageability, and photo-aging. Gives scalp and hair care advice and surveys anti-aging hair ingredients (minoxidil, glycolic acid, coconut oil, L-arginine, UV filters) and market products.

nodes.label: Intrinsic Aging
nodes.summary: Chronological aging driven by genetics and hormones; in hair it causes graying from lower melanin production and androgenic hair loss.

nodes.label: Extrinsic Aging
nodes.summary: Environmentally driven aging from UV, pollution, smoking, diet and lifestyle that degrades hair via lipid oxidation, disulfide cleavage, amino acid and melanin degradation.

nodes.label: Photo-Aging of Hair
nodes.summary: UV-induced damage causing lipid oxidation, disulfide cleavage, tryptophan degradation and cysteic acid formation; hair becomes dry, porous, weak, rough and lighter.

nodes.label: Hair Breakage
nodes.summary: Fiber fracture associated with dryness, loss of sebum, chemical relaxer misuse and weak disulfide network.

nodes.label: Frizz
nodes.summary: Hair fibers out of synchrony with the bundle, from damaged shape memory, cuticle damage raising inter-fiber friction, or static fly-away; common after bleaching and hot ironing.

nodes.label: Hair Manageability
nodes.summary: Ease of combing and styling, governed largely by cuticle friction; decreases with aging and damage.

nodes.label: Minoxidil
nodes.summary: Pharmacological hair-loss treatment applied as 2% or 5% scalp solution or 5% foam twice daily; 5% was 45% more effective than 2% after 48 weeks in men.

nodes.label: Pseudo-Catalase PC-KUS
nodes.summary: Narrow-band UV-activated pseudo-catalase that reduced epidermal H2O2 and repigmented eyelashes and skin in a University of Bradford study.

nodes.label: Methionine Sulfoxide Reductase
nodes.summary: MSR A and B enzymes that repair H2O2 damage; absent/lower in gray hair, contributing to graying.

nodes.label: Free Radical Theory of Graying
nodes.summary: Theory by Arck et al. that melanocyte apoptosis from oxidative stress in the pigmentary unit causes graying.

nodes.label: Glycolic Acid
nodes.summary: Alpha hydroxy acid (DuPont Glypure) that penetrates the hair shaft, conditioning, moisturizing, strengthening and preventing breakage, and exfoliates the scalp to reduce flaking.

nodes.label: Alpha Hydroxy Acid
nodes.summary: Acids such as glycolic acid cited as anti-aging hair ingredients benefiting shaft and root.

nodes.label: Coconut Oil
nodes.summary: Lauric acid triglyceride with high affinity for hair proteins that penetrates the shaft due to low molecular weight and linear chain; excellent conditioner.

nodes.label: Lauric Acid
nodes.summary: Principal fatty acid of coconut oil triglycerides.

nodes.label: Avocado Oil
nodes.summary: Highly emollient, moisturizing oil, good for dry and frizzy hair.

nodes.label: Jojoba Oil
nodes.summary: Oil providing nourishing, conditioning and shine benefits to hair.

nodes.label: L-Arginine
nodes.summary: Amino acid nitric oxide precursor (Ajinomoto) reported to stimulate hair regrowth and strengthen hair by nourishing roots.

nodes.label: Hair Sunscreen
nodes.summary: UV filters in shampoos, conditioners and sprays that prevent keratin breakdown and dye fading, e.g. Crodasorb UV-HPP, PARSOL SLX, ChromAveil.

nodes.label: PARSOL SLX
nodes.summary: Silicone-based UV-B absorber (DSM) preventing color fading, enhancing gloss and conditioning.

nodes.label: Crodasorb UV-HPP
nodes.summary: Polyester polyquaternized UV-B protectant substantive to hair (Croda).

nodes.label: Procapil
nodes.summary: Sederma active that reinforces hair anchoring and reduces hair loss.

nodes.label: Silicones
nodes.summary: Well-established hair care ingredients for shine; reduce inter-fiber friction so hair recovers permanent shape.

nodes.label: Quaternary Ammonium Compounds
nodes.summary: Cationic conditioners providing ease of combing.

nodes.label: Polyquaternium
nodes.summary: High-molecular-weight cationic polymers used for conditioning and thickening; polyquaternium-4, -11 and -37 also used in styling.

nodes.label: Polyvinylpyrrolidone
nodes.summary: PVP, a styling polymer for shaping hair, used in gels and mousses.

nodes.label: Peptides
nodes.summary: Small-molecular-weight peptides used as anti-aging hair ingredients; bioactive peptides also used in second-generation lash conditioners.

nodes.label: Ceramide
nodes.summary: Lipid of the cuticle and CMC (with fatty acids and cholesterol) and an anti-aging hair ingredient.

nodes.label: Shampoo
nodes.summary: Cleansing product; mild moisturizing shampoos recommended, avoiding harsh surfactants like SLS; silicone 2-in-1 shampoos let hair dry into its natural shape.

nodes.label: Hair Conditioner
nodes.summary: Product that conditions, smooths and lowers friction; after-color conditioners used post-dyeing.

nodes.label: Hair Colorant
nodes.summary: Permanent and demi-permanent dyes used to cover gray; permanent color oxidizes proteins and lipids via ammonia and H2O2.

nodes.label: Hair Relaxer
nodes.summary: Alkaline (pH 11.5-14) or thio/sulfite creams that permanently straighten curly hair; the most damaging permanent reshaping treatment.

nodes.label: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
nodes.summary: Harsh surfactant to avoid in daily cleansing because it strips natural oils.

nodes.label: Ammonia
nodes.summary: Alkalizer in permanent hair color that with H2O2 causes oxidative damage; absent in demi-permanent color.

nodes.label: Antioxidant Enzymes
nodes.summary: Endogenous superoxide dismutase, catalase and glutathione peroxidase that neutralize free radicals; decline with age.

nodes.label: Dandruff
nodes.summary: Scalp flaking most common with oily scalps; managed with anti-dandruff shampoos.

nodes.label: Hair Porosity
nodes.summary: Increase in fiber porosity caused by sunlight and photo-damage.

nodes.label: Tryptophan
nodes.summary: Amino acid in hair degraded by UV exposure and heat.

nodes.label: Cysteic Acid
nodes.summary: Oxidation product of cystine formed in photo-aged and alkaline-treated hair.

nodes.label: Cysteine
nodes.summary: Sulfur-rich amino acid involved in pheomelanin synthesis; hair is rich in half-cystine.

nodes.label: Tyrosine
nodes.summary: Amino acid oxidized by tyrosinase to form melanin.

nodes.label: Mechanisms of Changes in Hair Shape
nodes.summary: Treats hair as a shape memory biopolymer and explains temporary and permanent shape changes by water-setting, hot irons, thioglycolate perms and alkaline relaxers via a three-step soften-impose-lock mechanism. Also covers grooming dynamics, volume, frizz, body and styling polymers (Tg, welding seams, adhesion).

nodes.label: Shape Memory Polymer
nodes.summary: Polymers able to memorize a permanent shape, be fixed in a temporary shape and recover on a stimulus (heat, moisture, light, electricity); hair behaves as a semi-crystalline cross-linked SMP.

nodes.label: Water-Setting
nodes.summary: Temporary shape change by wetting to break hydrogen bonds in the gel structure, imposing a shape on rollers and rapidly drying to re-form them; reversed by re-wetting and slowly lost by stress relaxation.

nodes.label: Hydrogen Bond
nodes.summary: Weak bonds in the hair gel structure broken by water and re-formed on drying; store temporary shapes in water-setting and volumizing.

nodes.label: Hot Iron Styling
nodes.summary: Flat or curling irons at 160-230°C that dehydrate hair, partially melt crystalline keratin and soften the amorphous matrix above Tm/Tg, locking shapes by vitrification on cooling; causes damage.

nodes.label: Vitrification
nodes.summary: Hardening of the softened amorphous phase on cooling below Tg that locks in hot-iron temporary shapes.

nodes.label: Protein Denaturation
nodes.summary: Irreversible loss of native keratin conformation (crystalline melting above Tm, alkaline attack); removes permanent shape memory and weakens hair.

nodes.label: Differential Scanning Calorimetry
nodes.summary: DSC detects the hair crystalline melting endotherm and denaturation enthalpy, which drops 30-50% after alkaline relaxers.

nodes.label: Permanent Waving
nodes.summary: Breaking disulfide bonds with 7-9% ammonium or sodium thioglycolate at pH ~9.5, winding on rollers, and reoxidizing with 3% hydrogen peroxide to curl hair; quasi-permanent with gradual reversion.

nodes.label: Ammonium Thioglycolate
nodes.summary: Reducing agent whose thiolate ion selectively unzips disulfide bonds in perms (7-9%, pH ~9.5) and Thio relaxers.

nodes.label: Shape Reversion
nodes.summary: Gradual return to original shape after perms or relaxers because residual memory in primary/secondary protein structure and crystalline regions is not erased.

nodes.label: Disulfide Bond Interchange
nodes.summary: Rearrangement of disulfide cross-links that, with residual stresses, drives shape reversion and stores temporary shapes in the matrix.

nodes.label: Anfinsen Ribonuclease Experiment
nodes.summary: C. Anfinsen showed scrambled ribonuclease with re-formed disulfides could regain native shape with traces of mercaptoethanol/urea, explaining perm reversion.

nodes.label: Urea
nodes.summary: Additive to thioglycolate solutions that enhances hydrogen bond breakage, apparently improving perm efficiency.

nodes.label: Sodium Hydroxide
nodes.summary: Strong base of lye relaxers supplying OH ions at pH 11.5-14 (1.5-3%).

nodes.label: Lithium Hydroxide
nodes.summary: Strong base used in no-lye alkaline relaxers.

nodes.label: Guanidine Hydroxide
nodes.summary: Relaxer base generated in situ from calcium hydroxide and guanidine carbonate (mix/no-lye relaxers).

nodes.label: Sodium Bisulfite
nodes.summary: Sulfite reagent of 'Japanese' straightening, more selective to disulfide bonds but prone to shape reversion in tight curls.

nodes.label: Formaldehyde
nodes.summary: Cross-linker used with hot irons in 'Brazilian' straightening for almost permanent shape change; potential carcinogen banned in cosmetic use.

nodes.label: Lanthionine
nodes.summary: Thioether cross-link formed from cystine and OH ions during alkaline relaxing; proposed to lock in the straight shape.

nodes.label: Supercontraction
nodes.summary: Strong contraction of hair/wool in high-pH solutions; proposed to aid imposition of straight shape in relaxing.

nodes.label: Petrolatum
nodes.summary: Applied to scalp before 'base' relaxers to protect against irritation; pre-formulated in no-base relaxers.

nodes.label: Citric Acid
nodes.summary: Acid in neutralizing shampoos that stops OH ion reactions after relaxing.

nodes.label: Inter-Fiber Friction
nodes.summary: Friction between hair fibers balancing bending forces; high friction or polymer welds fix shapes, low friction (silicones) lets fibers slip and recover permanent shape.

nodes.label: Hair Volume
nodes.summary: Space occupied by a hair bundle beyond its nominal volume while fibers stay aligned in synchrony; created dynamically by water-setting in motion, friction, polymers, back-combing or static.

nodes.label: Back-Combing
nodes.summary: Teasing that lifts cuticle cells to interlock fibers, raising friction to create volume; effective but very damaging.

nodes.label: Static Fly-Away
nodes.summary: Electrostatic repulsion from negative charge transferred from rubber combs (triboelectric series); adds volume but causes frizz and dissipates with moisture.

nodes.label: Triboelectric Series
nodes.summary: Ranking of insulators by electron transfer; hair lies below rubber, so combing transfers electrons and charges hair negatively.

nodes.label: Hair Body
nodes.summary: Perception of abundant strong hair best described by bundle flexural rigidity, depending on fiber density, protein density, inter-fiber friction and temporary shapes.

nodes.label: Flexural Rigidity
nodes.summary: Mechanical property combining bending modulus and shape; coiled fibers and high friction raise bundle flexural rigidity and body.

nodes.label: Styling Polymers
nodes.summary: Film formers (PVP, VP/VA, acrylates, polyquaterniums, chitosan) that form seam and spot welds between fibers to restrict movement and hold temporary shapes without altering hair memory.

nodes.label: Polymer Seam and Spot Welding
nodes.summary: Junctions of dried styling polymer between fibers that restrict inter-fiber motion and give rigidity; depend on polymer Tg, moisture plasticization and adhesive strength.

nodes.label: Hair Spray
nodes.summary: Aerosol styling polymer in ethanol/water; low plasticization and fast evaporation rapidly harden welding spots to entrap shapes in motion.

nodes.label: Hair Gel
nodes.summary: Water-based pseudoplastic styling polymer formulation with high zero-shear yield stress; forms thick uniform seams for extreme styles.

nodes.label: Mousse
nodes.summary: Water-based styling polymer foam that partly plasticizes hair and provides uniform welding patterns.

nodes.label: VP/VA Copolymer
nodes.summary: Styling polymer listed for sprays and mousses.

nodes.label: Chitosan
nodes.summary: Natural polymer listed among hair styling polymers (also chitosan PCA).

nodes.label: Volatile Organic Compound Restrictions
nodes.summary: Restrictions on VOCs in aerosol formulations pushing development of water-soluble styling polymers.

nodes.label: Hair Drying Rate
nodes.summary: Rate of water evaporation controlling hydrogen bond re-formation; fast drying locks shapes in motion and builds volume.

nodes.label: Blow-Drying
nodes.summary: Rapid drying that locks water-set shapes and volume; also causes thermal stress and cuticle buckling.

nodes.label: Bed Hair
nodes.summary: Temporary shape locked in by stress relaxation in the gel structure during sleep or hat wearing at room temperature.

nodes.label: Apparent Permanent Shape
nodes.summary: Everyday hair shape, a quasi-permanent water set from fiber weight and inter-fiber interactions; real shape seen on water immersion (many wavy Caucasian fibers coil into circles).

nodes.label: Chemical Burn
nodes.summary: Skin burns from highly alkaline relaxer processes; area needing improvement.

nodes.label: Hair Thermal Conductivity
nodes.summary: Hair is a poor heat conductor; fibers 100 µm below the iron plate sense 20-25°C less, and the far side of a 1 mm swatch ~60°C less.

nodes.label: Eyelashes: Anatomy and Lash Conditioners
nodes.summary: Describes eyelash anatomy, glands and the short lash growth cycle, then the history and safety of lash conditioners, notably the prostaglandin analogue dechloro ethylcloprostenolamide. Reports clinical study results and newer peptide and adipose stem-cell-derived conditioners.

nodes.label: Keratin 38
nodes.summary: Keratin whose asymmetric distribution in the eyelash bulb produces the curved fiber.

nodes.label: Zeis Gland
nodes.summary: Unilobular sebaceous glands at the eyelid margin secreting oil into lash follicles.

nodes.label: Moll Gland
nodes.summary: Modified apocrine sweat glands surrounding eyelash follicles.

nodes.label: Meibomian Gland
nodes.summary: Eyelid sebaceous glands secreting lipid to form the tear film.

nodes.label: Lash Conditioner
nodes.summary: Topical eyelash growth products: oil/vitamin formulas (2000s), prostaglandin analogues (2007), then bioactive peptide and adipose stem-cell peptide generations; increase anagen lashes from 20 to 90%.

nodes.label: Prostaglandin Analogues
nodes.summary: Glaucoma drugs (latanoprost, bimatoprost) with hypertrichotic side effects increasing eyelash length, number and thickness; rare iris pigmentation and periocular darkening.

nodes.label: Dechloro Ethylcloprostenolamide
nodes.summary: Synthetic topical prostaglandin analogue (MD Lash Factor, 2007); increased lash length 1.44-1.94 mm vs 0.63 mm placebo in 4 weeks; non-irritating, nonmutagenic, no IOP change.

nodes.label: Latanoprost
nodes.summary: Glaucoma prostaglandin analogue increasing lash length 0.67-0.8 mm and thickness; described for alopecia areata.

nodes.label: Bimatoprost
nodes.summary: Ophthalmic prostaglandin analogue causing transient hyperemia; gave minimal lash enhancement in an alopecia areata patient.

nodes.label: Glaucoma
nodes.summary: Eye disease treated with prostaglandin analogue drops whose side effect is eyelash growth.

nodes.label: Alopecia Areata
nodes.summary: Autoimmune patchy hair loss; latanoprost described for it and one patient's lashes grew 100% with dechloro ethylcloprostenolamide.

nodes.label: Iris Pigmentation
nodes.summary: Rare side effect of ophthalmic prostaglandins; not observed in 70,000 dechloro ethylcloprostenolamide users.

nodes.label: Repeat Insult Patch Test
nodes.summary: Human RIPT on 209 subjects showed no irritation or sensitization for dechloro ethylcloprostenolamide.

nodes.label: Local Lymph Node Assay
nodes.summary: LLNA test negative for delayed dermal sensitization of the lash ingredient.

nodes.label: Ames Test
nodes.summary: Mutagenicity test in five Salmonella strains showing dechloro ethylcloprostenolamide is nonmutagenic.

nodes.label: Adipose-Derived Stem Cell Peptides
nodes.summary: Third-generation lash/hair actives: proteins secreted by adipose-derived stem cells; scalp hair reportedly regenerated after topical application.

nodes.label: Cyclic AMP
nodes.summary: Regulation of intracellular c-AMP suggested but unproven as lash conditioner mechanism.

nodes.label: MD Follicle Energizer
nodes.summary: Lash-conditioner-derived scalp product; 71% of 30 subjects agreed it helped hair growth; proposed as adjuvant to hair loss therapy.

nodes.label: Hamilton and Ludwig Scales
nodes.summary: Grading scales for male (Hamilton II-III) and female (Ludwig I-2 to I-4) hair loss used to enroll study subjects.
